title: Handle incomplete trailing SmolTalk turns in production SFT
description:
The pinned real SmolTalk training parquet contains conversations ending in an unmatched user message (first observed at source row 220). Nanochat's pinned adapter accepts these when the sequence alternates correctly and already contains a complete user/assistant turn, but this repository adds an incompatible last-message-must-be-assistant check and aborts before step 1. Remove only that extra restriction while retaining strict role/content validation and the requirement for at least one supervised turn.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load the pinned real SmolTalk training parquet through the production SFT normalization path.
2. Reach an alternating conversation with at least one complete user/assistant turn followed by an unmatched user message, first observed at source row 220.
3. Observe the repository reject the otherwise valid row at its extra final-assistant check before the first optimizer step, while the pinned nanochat adapter accepts and masks the trailing user context.
design: The pinned nanochat SmolTalk adapter requires at least two non-system messages and strict user/assistant alternation, but does not require the final role to be assistant. Preserve the trailing user message as masked context; do not trim, skip, or mutate source rows, and keep stable row identities.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test reproduces a SmolTalk conversation with one or more complete user/assistant turns followed by an unmatched user turn; normalization preserves the complete alternating conversation exactly, matching the pinned nanochat adapter; conversations with no complete turn and malformed/non-alternating content still fail with source context; focused SFT source/loader/CLI tests pass; the real cached SmolTalk source can yield through the previously failing row.
notes:
Discovered by gpt-training-sandbox-e3u. PR https://github.com/bjlkeng/gpt-training-sandbox/pull/83 at commit cbdd6ab. Red/green regression added for alternating SmolTalk conversations ending in a user turn; implementation removes only the incompatible final-assistant restriction. Validation: 71 focused SFT tests passed; Ruff passed; full downloaded-cache integration scan validated all 460,341 train and 24,229 test rows, preserving 258 train and 10 test rows with trailing masked user turns. Branch remains in_progress awaiting review/merge; the requested experiment is being run against this exact PR commit as extended integration validation.

Final feature head ad720ce1b663cbd8d515b609d0f03d53beeeb012 is an ancestor of origin/main, and local main was fast-forwarded to the merge. GitHub reported no configured status checks. Existing focused validation and the complete cached-source scan remain recorded above. Closing this blocker unblocks the active experiment bead gpt-training-sandbox-e3u.

title: Implement pinned CORE evaluation protocol
description:
Implement the pinned 22-task nanochat/DCLM CORE protocol end to end: strict bundle loading and provenance, prompt rendering and model scoring, centered aggregation, deterministic bounded subsampling, standalone base-evaluation integration, and a rough reference comparison artifact.

Plan ticket coverage: EVAL-007 through EVAL-009.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Pin nanochat commit 41865401f73ff1c5321ae53297bceb2b78d4c8b4, scripts/base_eval.py SHA-256 644083a99ded710f677b25168ca76fd0416dc7ef3890d346a72f76a20bb522fe, nanochat/core_eval.py SHA-256 9303997ff17fa48ad5e5730f33b7e79a687cc2a1fdad928666bb63dc3514c51d, and eval_bundle.zip SHA-256 90a7c19e28ee7a52b4f6e1f87658deb9fde7f63deba2379045bdb1fe9ea5d200. Treat the 22-task order, paths, baselines, prompt delimiters, few-shot seed 1234 plus shuffled task index, bounded shuffle seed 1337, truncation, mean-continuation-loss scoring, exact-token LM scoring, and centered formula as nanochat_core_v1. Evaluation reads an explicit local bundle and never downloads or mutates data implicitly. Keep typed bundle/domain contracts, prompt construction, tensor scoring, checkpoint composition, and artifact rendering in separate modules. Full runs cover all task rows; max-per-task runs are deterministically bounded, validate the few-shot pool, and remain visibly non-comparable to full results. Save a deterministic reference-comparison report from the pinned bundle CSVs and never present bounded deltas as full-run rankings.
acceptance_criteria:
- A strict loader accepts exactly the pinned 22-task core.yaml order and supported multiple_choice, schema, and language_modeling JSONL shapes; validates unique labels, safe relative paths, one baseline per task, file identities, and pinned bundle identity; and reports missing or malformed artifacts without network access.
- Prompt fixtures match the pinned nanochat rendering and seeded few-shot selection for every task type; BOS-prefixed tokenization, left truncation, continuation spans, BOS padding masks, mean continuation loss for categorical tasks, and exact-token language-model accuracy are tested on CPU.
- The centered formula is exactly (accuracy - 0.01 * random_baseline) / (1 - 0.01 * random_baseline), rejects non-finite or invalid values, and the aggregate is the unweighted mean over the complete configured task set.
- --eval core works independently and in core,bpb,sample order from one checkpoint; --core-bundle is explicit, --max-per-task uses deterministic seed-1337 subsampling and cannot masquerade as a full run, and failures install no partial report.
- base_eval.json records protocol/version/reference commit and files, bundle/config identities, checkpoint/tokenizer identities, per-task raw accuracy/baseline/centered/counts, aggregate, full versus bounded scope, timing, and max-per-task.
- A deterministic Markdown comparison artifact includes pinned GPT-2 family references from the bundle and clearly labels rough full-run versus bounded/non-comparable results. Tiny fake-bundle and fake-model tests cover success, ordering, truncation, insufficient few-shot pools, malformed data, identity mismatch, and atomic cleanup.

title: Make document-packing planner scale to ClimbMix
description: The default small_45m_3090 config uses the packed loader, but its best-fit epoch planner scans every existing row for every document. On the real 16-shard tokenized ClimbMix set (1,354,752 train documents, 871,904,857 tokens, and 253,183 continuation pieces), startup remained at 100% of one CPU core for more than three minutes with zero GPU use and no first batch; the stack was in _place_best_fit_piece. This makes the shipped production preset operationally impractical and forces a flat-loader override.
design: Preserve the exact deterministic best-fit placement semantics while replacing the linear scan over all existing rows with a capacity-indexed or otherwise bounded lookup. Since row capacity is seq_len + 1, exploit the bounded capacity domain and retain deterministic earliest-row tie behavior. Keep the current implementation or a simple oracle for differential tests.
acceptance_criteria: - Packed plans exactly match the existing reference algorithm for randomized small corpora, oversized documents, equal-fit ties, empty documents, padding rows, and fixed seeds. - Planner complexity does not grow quadratically with the number of documents; a deterministic regression proves existing-row count does not add a full scan per placement. - The 16-shard small_45m_3090 manifest can construct its first train batch in a documented bounded time and memory envelope on CPU, with progress or diagnostics sufficient to distinguish planning from a hang. - Packed loader state/resume, loss masks, continuation context, epoch determinism, and flat-loader behavior remain unchanged. - Focused data/pretraining tests and repository quality gates pass.
notes:
Implementation is review-ready. Summary: replaced the quadratic packed-row scan with a residual-capacity bitset and earliest-row heaps while preserving exact best-fit placement, continuation context, masks, padding, seeded epochs, and state format v2; added deterministic work counters and visible 100,000-document CLI milestones; documented the real production envelope. title: Estimate model size tokens per step and VRAM
description:
Add preflight resource estimates that explain each preset's unique parameter count, exact optimizer-step token budget, and conservative training-memory components before a GPU run starts.

Plan ticket coverage: SCALE-004, SCALE-005, SCALE-006.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Build pure estimators from the resolved config and documented single-process assumptions. Parameter size must deduplicate tied weights and separate trainable/non-trainable values. Tokens per microbatch/optimizer step must share the exact accumulation derivation used by training and distinguish processed model tokens from supervised targets. The VRAM estimate must itemize parameters, gradients, optimizer states, activations, logits/loss workspace, and a labeled allocator/headroom allowance for the configured dtype, batch, sequence, depth, width, and vocabulary. It is a conservative planning estimate, never an allocation guarantee. Expose the structured result in pretrain dry-run and compare it with optional actual snapshots through the foundation memory helper.
acceptance_criteria:
- Smoke, tiny-20M, and small-45M configs produce deterministic unique/trainable parameter counts that agree with constructed tied-weight models and identify embedding-dominated size.
- The token calculator returns device_batch_size * seq_len per microbatch and the exact configured total_batch_size_tokens per optimizer step, rejecting non-divisible or contradictory accumulation settings.
- VRAM output itemizes every documented component and assumption in bytes/MiB, includes explicit headroom, and never labels the estimate as observed usage or silently assumes AMP/activation checkpointing.
- Dry-run prints machine-readable and human-readable resource summaries without allocating the full training graph; JSON values are finite and stable.
- Fake/CPU tests cover tied versus untied weights, dtype changes, batch/sequence scaling, overflow/bad config, and component arithmetic; conditional CUDA comparison reports estimate versus actual without asserting a brittle ratio.
notes:
Implemented config-only GPT parameter estimation with tied-weight deduplication and trainability summaries, exact shared token-budget derivation, conservative itemized VRAM bytes/MiB with explicit dtype/manual-attention/no-AMP/no-checkpointing/no-compile/single-process assumptions, 20%-or-512-MiB allocator headroom, signed-64-bit overflow checks, optional estimate-versus-observed accelerator comparisons, and pretrain machine/human preflight output before model construction. Validation: full pytest 742 passed; dedicated pretraining integration 1 passed; conditional CUDA snapshot comparison passed on the available host; ruff format/check passed; mypy src scripts passed; uv lock --check and uv build passed. title: Orchestrate base evaluation modes reports and tracking
description:
Turn scripts.eval_base into the shared command boundary for independent BPB and fixed-sample execution, canonical base_eval.json output, and Tracker fan-out.

Plan ticket coverage: EVAL-003, EVAL-004, EVAL-010, EVAL-011.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Parse a strict normalized mode set and invoke immutable domain evaluators rather than embedding BPB or generation math in the CLI. Mode bpb runs both protocol implementations against the same checkpoint/tokenizer/manifest identities; sample runs the fixed prompt producer; core is a registered later capability and must fail explicitly until the Milestone 5 runner lands. Atomically write a schema-versioned metrics/base_eval.json that records requested/completed modes and full domain results, then pass finalized scalars/artifact paths to the Phase 10 reporting adapter. Partial or failed runs cannot masquerade as complete results.

- --eval accepts case-normalized deduplicated bpb, sample, and core values, rejects empty/unknown modes, and runs bpb or sample independently in deterministic requested order.
- bpb evaluates both nanochat_compat_v1 and full_documents_v1 against identical checkpoint/tokenizer/manifest/loss identities and publishes val_bpb namespaces without aliases or mixed ranking.
- core requests use a documented unavailable-capability error until the later CORE bead registers its runner; bpb/sample remain usable without CORE dependencies.
- metrics/base_eval.json is installed atomically with schema/version, requested and completed modes, checkpoint/config identities, both complete BPB result objects, sample metadata/path when requested, and explicit bounded/full-run status.
- Tracker receives only finalized eval/val_bpb, eval/val_bpb_full_documents, named retention scalars, and completed artifacts; JSONL remains available with W&B absent/disabled and no raw interactive prompts are logged.
- Subprocess and fake-domain tests cover each mode combination, strict errors, domain failure cleanup, identity mismatch, tracker parity, rerun conflicts, and deterministic JSON/Markdown paths.

title: Implement continuation-aware full-document BPB protocol
description:
Implement full_documents_v1 as a separate validation-domain protocol that scores every ordinary validation token and byte exactly once with continuation-aware context.

Protocol elaboration: complete-corpus base BPB.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Build a finite one-manifest validation iterator from the Phase 2 continuation policy: a document's first window starts with BOS, later windows carry the previous ordinary token as context, and only new ordinary tokens plus real document-boundary targets are supervised. Freeze document order, row packing, seed/config, and termination in the protocol version rather than inheriting whichever training loader settings happen to be active. The result exposes the common reference_commit field as null because this is a local protocol, while protocol_id/version and reference_config fully identify it. Publish only val_bpb_full_documents and eval/val_bpb_full_documents.
acceptance_criteria:
- One deterministic finite pass terminates after every validation document and counts each ordinary source token and raw byte exactly once as a target, including documents longer than sequence length and documents spanning shards.
- Carried context and residual padding add processed model tokens but no duplicate nats, counted targets, unique source coverage, or bytes; real BOS boundaries remain zero-byte special targets.
- The shared oversized-document fixture reports full token/byte retention of one and contrasts explicitly with nanochat_compat_v1 crop/discard output without calling that protocol's loader.
- Results require protocol_id full_documents_v1, null reference_commit, frozen local reference_config, and only the full-document metric namespaces; unsuffixed compatibility keys are rejected.
- Tests cover empty/Unicode/exact-fit/residual/multi-shard documents, batch padding, order reproducibility, coverage invariants, and no mutation of the training loader state.
notes:
Implemented deterministic full_documents_v1 finite manifest evaluation with capacity-indexed first-piece packing, continuation context from the previous ordinary token, exact one-time ordinary token/byte coverage, padding masks, reserved metric keys, frozen local provenance, and nanochat crop contrast tests. title: Implement pinned nanochat-compatible BPB protocol
description:
Implement nanochat_compat_v1 as an independent validation-domain protocol pinned to the exact upstream procedure needed for comparable unsuffixed BPB metrics.

Protocol elaboration: pinned nanochat-compatible base BPB.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Pin karpathy/nanochat commit 41865401f73ff1c5321ae53297bceb2b78d4c8b4 and record the relevant scripts/base_train.py, nanochat/dataloader.py, and nanochat/loss_eval.py settings. Reproduce final-validation-shard document order; tokenize in batches of 128 with BOS prepended; maintain a 1000-document buffer; fill each T+1 row by repeatedly taking the first largest document that fits, otherwise take the first shortest document, copy only its prefix to fill the row, and discard the remainder. Preserve resolved B, T, eval_tokens/steps, buffer, and tie behavior in reference_config. This protocol owns val_bpb and eval/val_bpb and must never call the continuation-aware loader.
acceptance_criteria:
- nanochat_compat_v1 records the exact pinned SHA and resolved evaluator config, follows final-shard/row-group/document order, and deterministically matches the frozen reference on ties, refill boundaries, multiple rows, and repeated validation cycles.
- Rows start with BOS, have T+1 tokens before x/y shifting, use first-largest-fit selection, and use first-shortest prefix crop/discard when no full document fits; no continuation from a cropped suffix is evaluated.
- The shared oversized-document fixture proves the exact retained prefix, discarded token/byte counts, processed model tokens, unique source coverage, and retention below one without affecting special-token byte totals.
- Results use only protocol_id nanochat_compat_v1 plus the reserved val_bpb and eval/val_bpb namespaces; no full-document key or loader alias is accepted.
- Network-independent tests vendor only minimal expected fixtures/provenance and compare the implementation with a clear frozen reference oracle; production code does not import nanochat.
notes:
Implemented nanochat_compat_v1 pinned to karpathy/nanochat commit 41865401f73ff1c5321ae53297bceb2b78d4c8b4 with immutable hashes for scripts/base_train.py, nanochat/dataloader.py, and nanochat/loss_eval.py. Reproduces final-shard row-group/document order, 128-document tokenization batches, 1,000-document whole-batch refill behavior, first-on-tie largest fit, first-shortest prefix crop/discard, repeated cycles, exact source coverage, and reserved val_bpb plus eval/val_bpb keys without importing nanochat or training loaders. title: Define token-byte BPB accumulation and result contracts
description:
Implement the shared, protocol-neutral bits-per-byte arithmetic and immutable coverage result used by both base-validation protocols.

Plan ticket coverage: EVAL-001, EVAL-002.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Accumulate unreduced cross-entropy nats only where targets are non-negative, explicitly supervised, and map to a positive entry in token_bytes; accumulate raw byte lengths from the same target positions. Keep packing and document-selection policy outside this kernel. Define one immutable result schema containing protocol id/version, nullable reference commit plus resolved reference config, checkpoint/tokenizer/manifest identities, source document/token/byte totals, processed model tokens, counted target tokens/bytes, unique source token/byte coverage, retention ratios, total nats, and BPB. Provide a shared oversized-document conformance fixture that protocol-specific beads consume.
acceptance_criteria:
- A hand-computed toy example matches total_nats / log(2) / counted_target_bytes exactly, including multi-byte tokens.
- Special tokens with token_bytes[id] == 0, targets below zero, explicit padding/loss-mask positions, and carried context positions contribute neither nats nor bytes.
- token_bytes shape/type/range, target bounds, loss shape, non-finite losses, inconsistent coverage, and zero counted bytes fail before a report or tracker record is emitted.
- The immutable result validates identities, non-negative counts, total/unique/retention relationships, and deterministic JSON serialization without non-finite values.
- Chunked accumulation matches one-shot accumulation and restores model mode without changing parameters, gradients, optimizer, scheduler, RNG, or loader policy.
- One shared fixture includes an oversized Unicode document and ordinary/special/masked targets for both protocol implementations to prove against.
notes: Implemented strict one-shot/chunked token-byte BPB accumulation, a side-effect-contained protocol-neutral model evaluator, immutable validated coverage/result JSON contracts, and a shared oversized-Unicode conformance fixture. title: Measure training throughput FLOPs MFU and peak VRAM
description:
Produce reusable domain telemetry for base pretraining from actual optimizer-step work and explicit hardware assumptions, leaving Tracker responsible only for transporting the resulting scalars.

Plan ticket coverage: TRAIN-013, TRAIN-014, TRAIN-015, TRAIN-016.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.

title: Optimize regex BPE runtime encoding
description: Replace the production RegexBPETokenizer full merge-table sweep with rank-driven active-pair encoding. A real 32K ClimbMix evaluation measured only 21.2 encode tokens/second versus roughly 3.8M-4.2M for tiktoken baselines, making tokenized-data preparation impractical. Keep runtime encoding from scratch in Python; tiktoken remains evaluation-only.
design: Improve RegexBPETokenizer itself rather than adding a parallel tokenizer implementation. Precompute learned pair ranks once, encode each regex chunk by considering only active adjacent pairs, choose the lowest learned rank with deterministic left-to-right handling of equal-rank overlaps, and update only the merged node neighborhood. Retain the existing clear merge_pair/reference composition as a test oracle. Do not use tiktoken in runtime code.
acceptance_criteria:
- RegexBPETokenizer.encode no longer scans all learned merges for every regex chunk and updates only active adjacent-pair candidates.
- Optimized encoding exactly matches the reference rank sweep across hand-traced overlaps, randomized learned tokenizers, Unicode, whitespace, regex boundaries, explicit special tokens, and save/load round trips.
- Runtime tokenizer modules do not import or depend on tiktoken; optional GPT-2/cl100k evaluation remains unchanged.
- A deterministic complexity regression proves irrelevant vocabulary merges do not add full chunk scans, and a bounded real 32K artifact benchmark records a material encode-throughput improvement without a brittle CI timing threshold.
- Focused and repository quality gates pass, and data/pretraining integration continues to use identical token IDs.
notes:
Implementation is complete and review-ready.

Summary: replaced the production RegexBPETokenizer full learned-rank sweep with one constructor-time pair-rank map and a per-regex-chunk lazy rank heap over linked active nodes. The existing merge_pair composition remains the reference oracle; no runtime module imports tiktoken. title: Publish reproducible architecture ablation reports
description:
Extend the existing offline run-comparison surface with a reproducible architecture/optimizer ablation manifest and deterministic JSON/Markdown matrix.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Reuse compare_runs, config/checkpoint identities, validation BPB, CORE, training telemetry, and throughput reports. An ablation manifest names one baseline and flag/optimizer variants and declares the intended changed fields; validation rejects hidden config/data/tokenizer/protocol/hardware differences or displays them as blockers. Aggregate prior one-feature comparisons without loading model weights. Keep OmegaConf plus explicit manifests as the orchestration boundary; record a Hydra decision only if the completed matrix demonstrates a concrete need for multirun composition.
acceptance_criteria:
- A versioned manifest identifies baseline/variants, declared changed config fields, run directories, evaluation/benchmark protocols, and expected hardware policy with stable identity.
- Validation proves each one-feature comparison differs only in declared fields (plus unavoidable run names/code commits that are displayed), and refuses rankable deltas for incomplete, bounded-incompatible, tokenizer/data/protocol, token-budget, or hardware mismatches.
- JSON and Markdown report parameter counts/deltas, best/final nanochat-compatible and full-document BPB, CORE where present, training tokens/sec/MFU/time/FLOPs, peak memory, inference latency/cache bytes where relevant, and optimizer-state cost.
- Every ARCH-001 through ARCH-011 feature and MuonAdamW has an explicit result or clearly labeled missing/failed/not-run cell; absence is never converted to zero or a win.
- Reports distinguish measured values, arithmetic deltas, and interpretation; preserve raw source artifact links/identities; and are atomically reproducible without W&B or checkpoint loading.
- Fixtures cover valid and blocked matrices, same/different commit cases, tied parameter counts, null hardware metrics, ordering, Markdown escaping, and deterministic reruns; README documents the workflow and the evidence-based Hydra decision.

title: Add a single-GPU MuonAdamW experiment
description:

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Pin mathematical/reference behavior to karpathy/nanochat 92d63d4e8bb4df75c3b71618f31ddde2378b2bcd, but implement a readable single-process optimizer for the RTX 3090 target rather than distributed ZeRO or opaque fused kernels. Partition every trainable parameter exactly once: eligible 2-D hidden attention/MLP matrices use Muon; embeddings, LM head (including tied ownership), value embeddings, 0/1-D values, biases, norms, and experimental scalars use AdamW. Expose explicit group hyperparameters, momentum schedule, orthogonalization/variance policy, and initial_lr values. Present any deviations from pinned upstream as named protocol identity, not parity claims.
acceptance_criteria:
- Optimizer config selects adamw or muon_adamw and validates all AdamW/Muon group hyperparameters while preserving AdamW defaults.
- A structural partition report assigns every trainable Parameter exactly once, rejects duplicates/omissions/ineligible Muon tensors, handles tied/untied heads and optional architecture modules, and has stable group identity.
- Small fp32 matrix steps match a frozen local oracle for the declared pinned single-GPU Muon protocol, including momentum, orthogonalization, variance/weight-decay policy, and learning-rate scaling.
- One combined Optimizer-compatible state_dict round-trips all groups/buffers/steps; scheduler, AMP unscale/clip, checkpoint exact resume, and failure/skipped-step behavior remain correct.
- CPU tests cover tall/wide/square/degenerate matrices and finite updates; a tiny model overfits with MuonAdamW without NaNs.
- A bounded AdamW versus MuonAdamW run records BPB, throughput, peak memory, optimizer-state bytes, convergence curves, complete protocol/hyperparameters, and pinned/deviation identity; no distributed code or performance claim is included.

Store separate length-n_layer parameters so future optimizer groups can treat them differently. Make initialization an explicit named profile, including neutral 1/0 and the pinned depth-dependent schedule, and record it in config/checkpoint identity. Disabled mode must preserve the existing residual equations exactly.

Validate the small gate input width for tiny models, keep the feature off by default, and expose placement/parameter identities. Reuse GQA geometry and cached/full attention; do not fold value embeddings into the base token embedding or Q/K.

title: Add sliding-window causal attention
description:
Add an optional per-layer sliding causal window that reduces long-context attention work while retaining periodic and final full-context layers.

Plan ticket coverage: ARCH-008.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Expose one validated L/S layer-pattern contract inspired by pinned nanochat 92d63d4e8bb4df75c3b71618f31ddde2378b2bcd: L means full causal context, S means an explicit short left window, the pattern tiles over depth, and the final block is forced to L. Default L preserves baseline. Derive one per-layer window description consumed by manual, SDPA/Flash adapters, KV-cache reads, FLOP estimation, and reports. A window changes visibility only, not stored token positions or conversation cropping.
acceptance_criteria:
- Config validates a non-empty L/S pattern and positive short-window size not exceeding seq_len; default L yields full causal attention in every layer and final-layer-full behavior is explicit.
- Hand-calculated masks prove a token sees only itself plus the configured preceding window in S layers, never future tokens, while L layers match baseline exactly.
- Manual and supported optimized backends have close forward/gradient results for boundary lengths, and fallback rejects any provider that cannot honor the requested window instead of silently using full context.
- Cached decode reads the same logical window as full forward, produces matching logits, and reports physical cache capacity separately from bytes actually read.
- FLOP/resource estimates and benchmark identity account for each layer's effective window; shape, tiny-overfit, and checkpoint tests pass.
- A bounded L versus declared pattern comparison records BPB, training throughput, decode latency, cache-read bytes, and peak memory; README labels the feature experimental and keeps it off by default.

title: Add grouped-query attention
description:

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Add canonical n_kv_head geometry and reconcile the existing use_gqa placeholder: n_kv_head=n_head is ordinary MHA; a smaller divisor enables GQA. Split or otherwise represent Q versus K/V projections so output sizes are explicit, then expand K/V groups only where a backend requires it. KVCache stores compact KV heads. Provide a deterministic compatibility conversion for legacy fused qkv checkpoints when n_kv_head=n_head; never silently reshape an MHA checkpoint into a reduced-head model. Keep head_dim=n_embd/n_head.
acceptance_criteria:
- Config requires 1 <= n_kv_head <= n_head and n_head % n_kv_head == 0, makes use_gqa agreement explicit, and preserves existing MHA configs by default.
- Q has n_head heads, K/V have n_kv_head heads, grouped expansion maps each query-head group to the expected K/V head, and output remains (B,T,C).
- A hand-built reference matches forward and gradients for MHA, multi-group, and MQA cases across manual and supported optimized backends.
- Compact K/V cache shapes, byte accounting, prefill, and decode are correct and cached logits match full-prefix logits.
- Legacy fused-qkv MHA checkpoints convert losslessly with identical logits; reduced-head architecture mismatches fail clearly and new state keys round-trip.
- Tiny overfit plus a bounded n_kv_head=n_head versus reduced-head comparison records BPB, throughput, decode latency, cache bytes, peak memory, and parameter delta; README documents divisibility and compatibility.

acceptance_criteria:
- model.profile accepts simple_gpt and nanochat_depth; the latter requires positive depth, aspect_ratio, and head_dim and resolves the documented formula exactly, including round-up cases.
- Resolved n_layer/n_embd/n_head/seq_len feed model construction, parameter/resource estimates, OOM advice, config identity, checkpoints, dry-run output, and resume compatibility through one shared path.
- Explicit dimensions that contradict derived depth-profile values fail with a field-specific error rather than being silently ignored; simple_gpt configs and existing checkpoints retain current behavior.
- The resolved profile does not enable RMSNorm, RoPE, ReLU-squared, GQA, FlashAttention, KV cache, Muon, or other later features implicitly.
- Table-driven tests cover depths around head-dimension boundaries, invalid/overflowing values, serialization, overrides, save/load, and equality with an equivalent explicit GPTConfig.
- A documented bounded construction/throughput matrix reports parameter counts and resource estimates for representative depth values without launching a long training run or claiming compute-optimality.

title: Compare optimized training throughput and memory
description:
Extend the existing production training-throughput benchmark into an identity-matched baseline/variant comparison for Phase 12 optimizations.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-014.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Reuse benchmark_pretrain, TrainingStepTelemetry, accelerator-memory snapshots, and metrics/throughput_benchmark.json rather than adding another timing loop. Add a comparison manifest that freezes code/config/data/tokenizer/hardware and changes one declared optimization at a time. Separate AMP, attention backend, activation checkpointing, compile startup, and combined-profile results; record requested versus effective state and fallback. CI verifies arithmetic with fake clocks, while real performance claims require same-hardware bounded runs.
acceptance_criteria:
- The existing bounded benchmark can execute float32/manual baseline and declared AMP, SDPA, Flash/fallback, compile, activation-checkpointing, and combined variants through production training code.
- Every result records identical-or-different code/config/model/data/tokenizer/hardware identities, warmup/timed steps, processed tokens, elapsed time, tokens/sec, FLOPs/MFU basis, peak memory, startup/compile time, and requested/effective optimization states.
- A comparison artifact rejects mismatched uncontrolled identities, reports absolute and relative tokens/sec/memory deltas, and never labels fallback output as the requested backend.
- Timing continues to exclude loading, planning, validation, sampling, checkpoint I/O, tracker fan-out, and report writing; compiler cold start is reported separately.
- CPU/fake-clock tests verify orchestration and comparison arithmetic without speed assertions; explicit RTX 3090 commands produce bounded same-hardware evidence for supported variants.
- README guidance explains numerical-sanity checks, no-NaN expectations, measurement variance, fallback interpretation, and how to reproduce each comparison.

title: Integrate cached generation with shared inference
description:
Add prefill plus single-token cached decoding to the shared generation primitive and make CLI/web ChatEngine consumers select it without introducing a second sampler.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-011, PERF-012.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Refactor the existing batch/stream generation core so only model-logit acquisition differs between naive and cached modes. Prefill the exact cropped prompt once, then decode one sampled visible token at a time through KVCache. Keep sampling, per-row RNG, top-k/top-p, stop-token omission, max-token fallback, TokenEvent ordering, cancellation, model-mode restoration, and conversation transactions shared. Resolve the existing model.use_kv_cache placeholder into one canonical runtime policy that does not change trained parameter identity.
acceptance_criteria:
- One shared generation API exposes explicit naive and cached modes; scripts.sample, fixed SFT sampling, ChatEngine, terminal chat, and local web can use cache without owning sampling/cache loops.
- Cached greedy generation exactly matches naive token IDs, stop reason/ID, sampled-token count, and visible text over empty/immediate-stop, one-token, long-prompt, and max-token fixtures.
- Seeded stochastic cached and naive runs consume equivalent RNG steps and match under the documented batch semantics, or any unsupported batched case is rejected before mutation.
- Prefill runs once for the active prompt and every later model call has sequence length one; instrumentation proves no growing full-context forward occurs.
- Context bounds, learned-position offsets, assistant_end/BOS omission, cancellation/iterator close, failure rollback, model mode, RNG restoration, and generation lease semantics remain unchanged.
- Each generation owns and releases/reset its cache, and CPU integration tests cover terminal and web event parity plus cache overflow and repeated conversations.

title: Implement a bounded reusable KVCache
description:
Add the model-level key/value cache contract needed for efficient prefill and single-token decoding, with exact capacity, position, reset, and per-layer ownership.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-010.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Keep KVCache tokenizer- and sampler-free. Preallocate per-layer K/V storage on the model device/dtype with explicit batch, key/value head, head-dimension, and max-sequence metadata; track logical position without reallocating. Attention writes only its own layer and model forward advances a transaction exactly once. Learned positional embeddings use the cache offset, and later RoPE can consume the same position contract. Reset clears logical state without unnecessary full-buffer zeroing; bounds fail before partial writes.
acceptance_criteria:
- KVCache validates layer count, batch size, KV-head count, head dimension, capacity, device, and dtype and exposes stable shape/bytes-per-token metadata.
- Prefill writes every layer for T prompt tokens and advances the logical position once; decode accepts exactly one new token and appends K/V at the current position.
- Reset returns position to zero and prevents stale values from becoming visible; overflow, batch/shape/device/dtype mismatch, duplicate layer writes, and partial transactions fail before committed advancement.
- Cached attention uses the same learned-position offset and causal semantics as a no-cache forward and supports the effective manual/SDPA backend contract.
- Cache tensors and transient positions are absent from model/checkpoint state_dicts and are released with their inference transaction.
- Deterministic CPU tests inspect exact per-layer K/V values across prefill, decode, reset, capacity edge, failure rollback, and byte accounting.

title: Add activation checkpointing to transformer training
description:
Enable per-block activation checkpointing for larger single-GPU base and SFT runs without changing evaluation behavior, parameter identity, or exact checkpoint resume.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-009.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Apply torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint with use_reentrant=False at the GPT block boundary only while training with gradients enabled. Preserve dropout RNG behavior and keep inference, BPB, sampling, and cached decoding on ordinary forwards. The config switch changes activation retention, not module/state_dict structure. Reuse the shared base/SFT model path and extend resource/benchmark assumptions instead of creating a second model.
acceptance_criteria:
- train.activation_checkpointing and sft.activation_checkpointing enable the same per-block implementation and false preserves baseline forward/backward behavior.
- Checkpointed and ordinary runs with shared weights and controlled RNG produce close logits, loss, input gradients, and parameter gradients, including nonzero dropout.
- Evaluation, inference-mode generation, and no-grad BPB never invoke recomputation; state_dict keys, parameter counts, optimizer grouping, and checkpoint compatibility are unchanged.
- A tiny overfit and exact-resume fixture pass with checkpointing enabled, including gradient accumulation and mixed precision interaction.
- Invalid use or recomputation failure leaves optimizer/global step unchanged and yields an actionable error.
- A bounded conditional CUDA comparison records peak memory and tokens/sec for the same config with the switch off/on, and resource estimates identify the effective assumption without promising a fit.

title: Add an optional torch.compile training path
description:
Make torch.compile a real opt-in for base training, SFT, and bounded benchmarks while preserving canonical model/checkpoint identity and an observable eager fallback.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-008.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Wrap model compilation in one runtime adapter after canonical model construction and before execution. The uncompiled module remains the sole owner of state_dict, parameter grouping, checkpoint metadata, and architecture identity so compiler wrapper prefixes never leak into artifacts. Separate compilation/startup time from steady-state timing. Validate supported device/backend combinations and make any eager fallback explicit in policy, logs, and reports; compile remains off by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- train.compile and sft.compile use one adapter and no longer fail as unimplemented; false preserves the current eager path exactly.
- Compiled execution supports the shared training/evaluation boundaries without changing canonical state_dict keys, optimizer parameter ownership, checkpoint identity, or resume loading.
- Requested/effective compile state, backend/mode options, compile duration, recompilation observations, and fallback reason are recorded separately from timed steady-state work.
- Unsupported or failed compilation follows the configured explicit error/eager-fallback policy before a misleading completed run is published.
- Deterministic CPU tests use an injected compiler to cover wrapping, failure, fallback, checkpoint save/load, and no-op behavior; an available-device smoke performs forward/backward and a resumed optimizer step.
- The production benchmark excludes cold compilation from tokens/sec while preserving it as separately reported startup cost.

title: Add optional FlashAttention with observable fallback
description:
Add the optional flash attention backend behind lazy capability checks and provide deterministic fallback when the dependency, device, dtype, shape, or kernel is unavailable.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-006, PERF-007.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Extend the canonical backend enum rather than adding another boolean. Keep the core install and CPU imports free of a FlashAttention package. A small provider adapter performs preflight, chooses the supported flash kernel, and returns requested backend, effective backend, and fallback reason. On the target RTX 3090, unsupported upstream FA3 must fall back to PyTorch SDPA rather than fail or pretend flash ran; an explicitly strict mode may reject fallback before training. Sampling, cache, and model math stay outside the adapter.
acceptance_criteria:
- attention_backend=flash imports any optional provider lazily and normal installation, CPU tests, manual attention, and SDPA do not require it.
- Capability preflight covers dependency version, CUDA availability/capability, dtype, head dimension, dropout/training mode, causal/window support, and KV-cache support where requested.
- Supported flash execution preserves shared projection/state keys and matches SDPA forward and backward results on deterministic small tensors within dtype-specific tolerances.
- Unavailable or unsupported flash requests either follow the documented fallback policy to SDPA (then manual only if SDPA itself is unavailable) or fail before a run starts in strict mode.
- Requested/effective backend and a stable fallback reason enter config/report identities, logs, and benchmarks; no run is labeled FlashAttention when it used SDPA.
- Fake-provider tests cover success and every fallback class, while an opt-in long-sequence CUDA benchmark records time and peak memory without paid/network execution or a brittle CI threshold.

title: Add a selectable SDPA attention backend
description:
Add PyTorch scaled-dot-product attention as an explicit backend and prove forward, backward, masking, dropout, and training parity with the readable manual implementation.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-004, PERF-005.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Introduce one canonical attention-backend setting with manual as the compatibility default and sdpa as the optimized option; reconcile the existing future-facing use_flash_attention boolean without allowing contradictory config. Keep Q/K/V projection and output layout shared. SDPA uses is_causal for ordinary full causal attention and training-only dropout_p; never materialize the manual T-by-T mask on the optimized path. Preserve manual state-dict keys so the same checkpoint weights can run either backend.
acceptance_criteria:
- Validated config selects manual or sdpa unambiguously, defaults to manual, and loads existing configs/checkpoints without changing their effective behavior.
- Manual and SDPA modules share parameters and state_dict layout, preserve (B,T,C) shape, causal semantics, model mode, and configured attention/output dropout.
- Deterministic small-tensor forward and input/parameter-gradient comparisons are close under documented dtype tolerances, including one-token, exact-context, and nonzero-dropout fixtures.
- Future-token perturbation cannot affect earlier outputs on either backend, and invalid sequence/head/backend combinations fail actionably.
- A tiny overfit/training smoke succeeds through SDPA with finite loss and gradients on CPU or the available device.
- The existing production throughput protocol can identify the requested and effective backend for later before/after measurement; no benchmark result is fabricated by unit tests.

title: Add AMP and exact resumable GradScaler training
description:
Enable PyTorch autocast for practical reduced-precision base and SFT training, use GradScaler for float16, and preserve scaler state through exact checkpoint resume.

Plan ticket coverage: PERF-001, PERF-002, PERF-003.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Centralize precision behavior at the shared optimizer-step boundary used by pretraining, SFT, and the production benchmark. Keep parameters and optimizer state in their existing stable precision; float32 uses no autocast/scaler, float16 CUDA uses autocast plus torch.amp.GradScaler, and bfloat16 uses autocast without scaling. Scale before backward, unscale exactly once before gradient clipping, then step/update only at the optimizer boundary. Store a versioned scaler state beside optimizer/scheduler state and validate dtype/device compatibility on resume. Do not create separate base and SFT loops.
acceptance_criteria:
- train.dtype has explicit float32, float16, and bfloat16 runtime semantics; unsupported device/dtype pairs fail before model or checkpoint mutation.
- Base training, SFT, and benchmark execution use the same autocast/scaler policy, with float32 preserving the current path and defaults.
- Float16 loss is scaled before backward, gradients are unscaled once before clipping, skipped non-finite steps do not advance scheduler/global-step/checkpoint cadence, and scaler.update occurs at the documented boundary.
- Checkpoints record scaler enabled state and complete state_dict; exact resume rejects incompatible precision policy and reproduces uninterrupted model, optimizer, scheduler, RNG, loader, and scaler progression on deterministic fixtures.
- AMP smoke tests assert finite loss/gradients and no NaNs; fake autocast/scaler CPU tests cover call order, accumulation, clipping, skipped steps, save/load, and disabled behavior.
- A bounded conditional CUDA test records tokens/sec and peak memory for float32 versus supported AMP modes without imposing a flaky speed threshold or making a GPU a CI requirement.

title: Orchestrate chat evaluation and write chat_eval.json
description:
Replace the eval_chat stub with one bounded/full single-device orchestration path that composes the completed task evaluators, ChatCORE arithmetic, fixed-prompt diagnostics, and an atomic metrics/chat_eval.json report.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-012.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Keep scripts.eval_chat thin: resolve config/checkpoint/cache/task/scope/generation/code-execution options, load through the existing SFT checkpoint boundary, and call evaluation modules. Build one immutable report before writing. The report separates task accuracies, centered scores, aggregates, fixed-prompt diagnostics, identities, protocol/settings, scope, and failures. Write only a completed requested scope atomically; a full ChatCORE report requires every canonical task and fixed diagnostics. Leave tracker fan-out to the existing downstream tracking bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts.eval_chat has actionable help and validates the SFT checkpoint, tokenizer, task selection, batch/sample bounds, generation settings, cache roots, output directory, device, and code-execution opt-in before expensive work.
- The default full run executes the five canonical tasks plus fixed-prompt diagnostics; task filters and max-problems create an explicitly bounded/partial report with null full aggregates.
- metrics/chat_eval.json is atomically written under the run directory only from one immutable completed result and includes schema/version, status/scope, identities, settings, raw counts/accuracies, baselines, centered scores, ChatCORE values, and response diagnostics.
- Existing incompatible completed reports are not silently overwritten; same-identity reruns are deterministic and interruption or task failure leaves no completed artifact.
- The orchestration restores model mode and RNG state, remains single-process/single-device, and never duplicates task scoring, sampling, aggregate arithmetic, or tracker logic.
- CLI and CPU integration tests use local cached fixtures and a tiny deterministic checkpoint to cover full, task-filtered, bounded, failure, and code-execution-refusal paths with no network or GPU requirement.

title: Integrate fixed SFT prompts and response diagnostics
description:
Reuse the completed five-prompt SFT sample suite in chat evaluation and compute stop, response-length, empty-response, JSON, and code-format diagnostics from its immutable sample results.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-008, CHAT-EVAL-009, CHAT-EVAL-010, CHAT-EVAL-011.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: FIXED_SFT_PROMPTS, FixedSFTSamplingConfig, and FixedSFTSamplesResult remain the sole prompt and generation contracts; do not add another fixed-prompt list or sampler. Add pure diagnostics over completed samples. Define assistant-end stop rate separately from BOS safety stops, lengths in visible generated tokens, empty responses after Unicode whitespace trimming, strict whole-response JSON parsing for the JSON prompt, and explicit balanced/python/untyped/plain/malformed fence categories for the code prompt. Treat these as format diagnostics, never semantic correctness scores.
acceptance_criteria:
- Chat evaluation consumes the existing exact five ordered prompts and prompt-set identity and does not duplicate their rendering, sampling, stop, or artifact logic.
- Metrics include assistant_end stop count/rate, BOS safety-stop count, max-token count, visible-token mean/min/max, and empty-response count/rate with documented denominators.
- The JSON prompt reports whole-response parse validity, object type, and exact presence of name/age/city keys without silently extracting a JSON substring.
- The code prompt reports balanced python fence, balanced untyped fence, plain code, or malformed fence behavior under deterministic documented rules.
- Empty, immediate-stop, multibyte text, malformed JSON, extra JSON text, missing keys, and unmatched/multiple fence fixtures have exact expected results.
- Diagnostics serialize stably with checkpoint/tokenizer/renderer/prompt/generation identities and make no claim about answer quality.

title: Compute complete ChatCORE and ChatCORE_cat results
description:
Define the immutable ChatCORE result contract and calculate the full and categorical centered aggregates from completed task results.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-006, CHAT-EVAL-007.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Keep task execution separate from arithmetic. Use the roadmap's fixed ordered task set and baselines: 0.25 for ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and MMLU; 0.0 for GSM8K and HumanEval. Center each raw accuracy with (accuracy - baseline) / (1 - baseline), then take an unweighted mean over all five for ChatCORE and over the three categorical tasks for ChatCORE_cat. Preserve negative centered scores below baseline. Partial or failed task sets may be inspected but must not receive either full aggregate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A frozen result type accepts exactly the five canonical task names, raw passed/total/accuracy values, and matching execution identities.
- Centered task scores use the documented fixed baselines and formula with deterministic float behavior; scores below random baseline remain negative rather than being clipped.
- ChatCORE is the unweighted mean of all five centered scores and ChatCORE_cat is the unweighted mean of the three categorical centered scores.
- Duplicate, unknown, failed, zero-total, inconsistent-accuracy, or non-finite task results are rejected.
- Bounded all-task runs are explicitly labeled bounded; missing tasks produce a partial result with null aggregates rather than a misleading ChatCORE value.
- Hand-calculated fixtures cover random-baseline zeroes, perfect scores, below-baseline scores, mixed scores, input-order independence, and exact serialization round trips.

title: Add opt-in HumanEval-style code evaluation
description:
Add the HumanEval-style simple coding task on the shared generative evaluator, with strict dataset normalization, deterministic code extraction, and an explicit local code-execution safety boundary.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-005.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Pin adapter semantics to nanochat's openai/openai_humaneval test task, but do not present a Python subprocess as a security sandbox. The evaluator is disabled unless the operator explicitly opts into generated-code execution. Use an injected executor contract; the local implementation runs in a fresh temporary-directory subprocess with scrubbed environment, closed stdin, output/time/memory limits, and documented residual risk. Task code owns first-fence/plain-code extraction, required imports, tests, and entry-point assembly; the shared generative runner owns sampling.
acceptance_criteria:
- The strict cached task spec uses openai/openai_humaneval/openai_humaneval/test and validates prompt, canonical solution, test program, and entry point with stable row identity.
- Evaluation refuses before generation or execution unless generated-code execution is explicitly enabled, and CLI/help documentation states that the local runner is not safe for malicious adversarial code.
- Code extraction accepts the first python or untyped fenced block and otherwise trimmed plain code, preserves required leading imports, appends the test program and check(entry_point), and never executes the reference solution.
- Each execution uses a fresh process and temporary directory with a scrubbed environment, no stdin, bounded time, memory, and captured output; timeout, memory, syntax, test, and infrastructure failures remain distinguishable.
- Pass-any task accuracy uses the shared deterministic multi-sample runner and records execution-policy identity without placing generated programs in tracker metrics.
- Tests inject a fake executor for orchestration and include bounded harmless subprocess cases for success, assertion failure, timeout, excessive output, and cleanup; no untrusted code runs in CI by default.

title: Add shared generative chat evaluation and GSM8K
description:
Build the shared deterministic generative task runner and use it for GSM8K test evaluation with canonical chat rendering, shared sampling, and exact final-answer normalization.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-004.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Reuse the existing openai/gsm8k cached source, Conversation schema, render_completion_prompt, and shared generation primitive used by fixed SFT samples. Centralize per-problem/per-sample seed derivation, assistant_end plus BOS stopping, completion metadata, and pass-any aggregation in a task-neutral runner. GSM8K owns only strict row parsing and the pinned #### numeric-answer extractor; it must not copy the sampler or calculator execution behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- GSM8K uses the pinned openai/gsm8k main/test cache and deterministic seed-42 logical order without network access during evaluation.
- Ground truth and generated completions use one tested #### answer extractor that handles a leading minus, decimal point, and commas and returns no answer when the marker is absent.
- The generative runner renders a user-only canonical completion prompt, invokes the shared sampler with assistant_end and BOS stops, and derives stable independent seeds for every problem/sample.
- Per-task results record problem count, sample count, passed count, pass-any accuracy, generation settings, stop reasons, and all data/model/tokenizer/renderer identities without treating a bounded run as full.
- A problem passes iff at least one configured sample has the normalized reference answer; zero samples, incomplete generation, or scoring errors fail clearly.
- Network-free CPU tests cover correct/incorrect/missing answers, multiple samples, stop tokens, max-token completion, deterministic reruns, and failure cleanup without a second generation loop.

title: Add MMLU categorical chat evaluation
description:
Add the MMLU test adapter to the shared categorical chat-evaluation path, reusing the repository's existing MMLU cached source and small-model multiple-choice rendering semantics.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-003.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Promote or reuse one multiple-choice rendering helper so SFT normalization and chat evaluation cannot drift on choice=letter binding or whitespace. Consume the existing cais/mmlu all/test Hub cache contract, preserve subject metadata, and delegate all batching and answer-letter scoring to the categorical evaluator introduced for ARC. Do not create a second MMLU downloader, renderer, or scoring loop.
acceptance_criteria:
- MMLU evaluates the pinned cais/mmlu all/test cached source with deterministic seed-42 ordering and explicit bounded/full scope.
- Every row has a non-empty question, exactly four string choices, an answer index in [0, 3], and preserved subject metadata.
- Evaluation and SFT use one exact choice=letter prompt format with no whitespace before A/B/C/D, while evaluation omits the gold assistant message.
- The shared categorical runner produces exact overall passed/total/accuracy plus per-subject counts whose totals reconcile.
- Offline CPU fixtures cover all answer positions, multiple subjects, malformed rows, bounded views, and logits whose unrestricted vocabulary argmax differs from the constrained letter argmax.
- No task-specific model-forward or padding loop is added outside the shared categorical evaluator.

title: Add categorical chat evaluation and ARC tasks
description:
Build a reusable categorical chat-evaluation path on the existing cached-Hub, conversation-rendering, tokenizer, and SFT-checkpoint contracts, then add ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge adapters with exact answer-letter-logit scoring.

Plan ticket coverage: CHAT-EVAL-001, CHAT-EVAL-002.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Pin task behavior to karpathy/nanochat commit 92d63d4e8bb4df75c3b71618f31ddde2378b2bcd while keeping this repository single-process and offline-after-prepare. Reuse HubDatasetSpec/CachedHubParquetDataset and the canonical chat renderer. Task adapters own strict source normalization; one evaluator owns batching, BOS padding, true prompt-end indices, and answer-letter logit selection. Score only each example's declared choices, require every answer letter to encode as one token, and never sample text for categorical tasks. Preserve source, order, checkpoint, tokenizer, renderer, and bounded/full-run identities.
acceptance_criteria:
- ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge use strict cached-parquet specs for allenai/ai2_arc, the named subsets, and test split, with pinned source identity and no implicit network access during evaluation.
- Row normalization validates question text, aligned choice labels/text, and an answer key present in the available labels; seed-42 ordering and bounded slicing are deterministic.
- Prompts use the canonical chat completion renderer without leaking the ground-truth assistant answer.
- Batched scoring reads logits at each row's last real prompt token despite BOS right-padding and chooses only among that row's single-token answer letters.
- Immutable per-task results record passed/total counts, raw accuracy, dataset/protocol/model identities, and bounded versus full scope; failures cannot publish a completed result.
- CPU tests cover unequal prompt lengths, non-four-choice rows, invalid labels, multi-token letters, deterministic ties, mode restoration, and hand-computed logits.

title: Prove and document the local web acceptance path
description:
Add backend and real-browser acceptance coverage for the complete local web flow, then document it with reproducible launch guidance and representative UI screenshots.

Plan ticket coverage: WEB-026, WEB-027, WEB-030.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Use FastAPI TestClient or its supported equivalent for deterministic HTTP/WebSocket contract coverage with injected services, plus one headless browser smoke path against a live loopback server and tiny deterministic chat checkpoint. The smoke must remain network-free beyond loopback and CPU-capable. Produce documentation screenshots from the same controlled fixture/settings so they show an honest state and can be regenerated; do not make screenshots the sole behavioral evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused FastAPI client suite covers health/config, catalog/load, reset, tokenize/detokenize, transcript export, WebSocket completion, busy, cancel, malformed input, and sanitized errors against injected deterministic services.
- A headless browser smoke launches the actual web command on 127.0.0.1 with a tiny deterministic checkpoint, loads the page, sends a message, observes streamed text and metrics, stops a generation, resets, switches supported settings/checkpoints, opens token debug, and exports parseable JSONL.
- The browser smoke proves no request leaves loopback, requires no credentials or paid service, runs without CUDA, has bounded timeouts, captures useful diagnostics on failure, and shuts down the server/process tree reliably.
- README documents installation of the web extra, the exact local launch command, loopback default and explicit remote-bind warning, controls, checkpoint expectations, transcript/privacy behavior, and the deterministic smoke command.
- Representative desktop and narrow-viewport screenshots are generated from the controlled smoke fixture, contain no secrets or user data, are referenced by README, and have a documented regeneration path.
- Tests assert the terminal CLI and web backend both consume the same ChatEngine/TokenEvent contracts and contain no second generation loop.
- The full applicable unit/integration, lint, type, lock, and package-build gates pass with core-only and web-extra import boundaries covered.

title: Add web metrics, transcript export, and inspection controls
description:
Complete the local testing harness with displayed latency/throughput, explicit JSONL transcript export, checkpoint selection, raw-token inspection, and a renderer-aware prompt-template selector.

Plan ticket coverage: WEB-021 through WEB-025.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Compute display metrics from server monotonic timestamps and shared generation counts, reusing existing accelerator-memory helpers where applicable; the browser only formats finalized values. Export the canonical Conversation schema as downloadable UTF-8 JSONL instead of accepting arbitrary server write paths. Populate checkpoint and renderer choices from sanitized server capabilities. Keep raw-token/debug data local to the explicit panel. This bead creates the structured aggregate session boundary needed by TRACK-028 but does not publish raw prompts/responses or duplicate the privacy policy owned by gpt-training-sandbox-h2q.12.
acceptance_criteria:
- Terminal generation events expose and the page displays generated tokens, prefill latency, decode latency per sampled token, tokens/sec, and peak CUDA memory when available, with documented zero/empty/cancel semantics and fake-clock arithmetic tests.
- Transcript export returns a deterministic application/x-ndjson download using the canonical versioned Conversation schema; it round-trips through read_conversations, uses a safe filename, preserves Unicode, and excludes cancelled/failed partial turns.
- Explicit transcript export works independently of tracker settings and does not grant a client an arbitrary server filesystem write primitive.
- The checkpoint dropdown reflects the sanitized catalog, shows the active identity, performs an atomic load, and clears UI/session state only after success while preserving the prior session on failure.
- The raw-token panel is explicitly opt-in in the UI and shows prompt/generated IDs, stop metadata, and context-cropping counters from server events without rendering content as HTML or sending it to a tracker.
- The prompt-template selector is populated from checkpoint/server-supported renderer IDs, defaults to the canonical chat renderer, resets incompatible history on an acknowledged change, and rejects unsupported templates without client-side template reimplementation.
- Aggregate session values are exposed through one structured boundary with session/turn IDs; raw prompt and response records are neither constructed nor logged by default, leaving the four-way privacy matrix to gpt-training-sandbox-h2q.12.
- Focused backend/frontend tests cover metric consistency, transcript bytes, failed loads, selector resets, debug safety, and absence of sentinel raw content from metrics/artifacts.

title: Build the plain browser streaming chat experience
description:
Build the framework-free local chat page and wire its generation settings, streamed response rendering, stop/reset controls, and context-window display to the versioned backend contracts.

Plan ticket coverage: WEB-016 through WEB-020.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Serve tracked local HTML, CSS, and JavaScript assets with no CDN or build-time framework. Keep the browser as a pure protocol client: it sends settings and user actions, renders server-owned TokenEvent deltas, and never tokenizes, templates, crops, or infers completion locally. Use textContent and explicit DOM construction for untrusted model/user text. Drive control enabled/disabled state from acknowledged server lifecycle events so stop, reset, reconnect, busy, and error behavior is visible and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
- GET / serves a usable plain HTML chat page with local CSS/JavaScript assets and no remote fonts, scripts, styles, analytics, or network dependencies.
- The page exposes bounded temperature, top_k, and max_new_tokens controls whose normalized values are sent exactly once with each generation request and whose validation errors are shown without opening generation.
- User and assistant content is rendered with safe text nodes; streamed fragments appear in order without HTML execution, replacement corruption, duplicate text, or visible control tokens.
- Stop remains available during generation and sends cooperative cancellation; reset waits for server acknowledgement before clearing rendered state, and both controls recover correctly from busy, disconnect, and error outcomes.
- The context display shows current retained tokens versus model maximum plus any dropped-turn/truncated-token indicators from ChatState, and never estimates context independently in JavaScript.
- Input focus, labels, keyboard submit behavior, scrolling, status announcements, and disabled states support basic keyboard and screen-reader use.
- Frontend-focused tests validate DOM-safe rendering, protocol message construction, event ordering, control state transitions, and reconnect behavior without an external CDN or real GPU.

title: Stream cancellable generation through one WebSocket
description:
Expose shared ChatEngine generation as a versioned WebSocket protocol with lossless TokenEvent serialization, cooperative cancellation, and an immediate single-GPU busy rule.

Plan ticket coverage: WEB-011 through WEB-014.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Keep one application-owned generation lease rather than a queue. Validate a generation request before acquiring model state, append its user message once, and forward ChatEngine events without reconstructing text or sampling. Cancellation and disconnect must close the engine iterator cooperatively so its transaction and RNG/module cleanup run; the stop signal itself must never wait behind the generation lease. Serialize load/reset/checkpoint changes against active generation, and use stable protocol envelopes for token, metrics, done, cancelled, busy, and error outcomes.
acceptance_criteria:
- WS /ws/generate accepts a bounded typed request containing one user message plus supported GenerationConfig overrides and rejects malformed or unloaded requests before conversation mutation.
- Every streamed TokenEvent is serialized losslessly with a protocol version, event type, token ID, text delta, cumulative counts, timing fields, and terminal completion/stop metadata; transport code does not decode tokens independently.
- A completed stream has ordered token events followed by one terminal metrics/done outcome, and its visible text/IDs equal the assistant turn committed by ChatEngine.
- A stop request or client disconnect cooperatively closes generation, emits or records one cancelled outcome where possible, commits no partial assistant turn, releases model/RNG resources, and permits the next request.
- Exactly one generation owns the single-GPU lease; a concurrent request receives an immediate stable busy error rather than queuing or invoking the model.
- Load, reset, shutdown, failure, and cancellation paths cannot deadlock, leak the lease, mix events between sessions, or leave the engine marked active.
- Async tests with deterministic fake engines cover completion, assistant/BOS stops, max-token fallback, cancellation before/after tokens, disconnect, generator error, concurrent clients, and successful reuse after every terminal path.
- No handler contains a model-forward loop, sampling code, chat rendering, or duplicated stop-token logic.

title: Implement checkpoint and tokenizer session APIs
description:
Add the local checkpoint catalog, atomic checkpoint loading, session reset, and bounded tokenizer utility endpoints around one loaded ChatEngine.

Plan ticket coverage: WEB-006 through WEB-010.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Introduce one application service that owns the active ChatEngine and serializes state mutations. Enumerate only validated checkpoint candidates beneath the configured checkpoint directory, resolve containment and symlinks before loading, and never accept an arbitrary client filesystem path. Construct and validate a replacement SFT engine off to the side, then swap atomically so a failed load leaves the prior session usable. Tokenize/detokenize only through the active checkpoint tokenizer with typed payload and size limits.
acceptance_criteria:
- GET /api/checkpoints returns a deterministic sanitized catalog restricted to regular checkpoint files under the configured directory; traversal, symlink escape, unreadable, and malformed candidates cannot expose arbitrary host paths.
- POST /api/load_checkpoint accepts only a catalog identity, loads an SFT checkpoint and matching tokenizer through the shared loader/ChatEngine contract, and atomically swaps the active session after full validation.
- Failed or cancelled loads leave the previous checkpoint and conversation usable; a successful checkpoint change clears incompatible conversation state and reports checkpoint, tokenizer, renderer, device, and context identities without secrets.
- POST /api/reset delegates to the active ChatEngine and returns the resulting immutable public state; unloaded and busy states have stable typed errors.
- POST /api/tokenize and POST /api/detokenize use only the active tokenizer, preserve Unicode and special-token policy exactly, enforce bounded request/token sizes, and reject malformed IDs before mutation.
- The service has explicit unloaded, loading, ready, generating, and failed transition coverage and does not keep two models resident after a successful swap.
- Tests use fake checkpoint loaders and tokenizers to cover catalog ordering, path containment, atomic rollback/swap, reset, round trips, payload limits, and sanitized error shapes without loading Torch weights or opening a socket.

title: Establish the local-only FastAPI application boundary
description:
Turn the web command stub into a dependency-isolated, local-only FastAPI application boundary that consumes the shared ChatEngine and exposes the first versioned health/config contracts.

Plan ticket coverage: WEB-001 through WEB-005, WEB-015.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Treat the Phase 8 ChatEngine as the only inference owner; the web layer may adapt events but may not refactor a second generator into handlers. Preserve the existing optional web dependency group and keep FastAPI/Uvicorn imports out of normal package and non-web command paths. Build an app factory with injected service/engine factories and explicit lifespan ownership, without loading a checkpoint, allocating a GPU, opening a socket, or starting background work at import time. Enforce loopback at both validated config and command-launch boundaries; a non-loopback bind requires a conspicuous explicit opt-in.
acceptance_criteria:
- The web optional dependency group contains the minimal compatible FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn, and streaming dependencies needed by the implementation, while core installation, unit tests, and non-web commands work when they are absent.
- scripts.web_chat --help works without importing optional web packages; live execution without the extra fails with one actionable installation command and no traceback.
- create_app returns a fresh independently testable FastAPI application from injected configuration/services and performs no checkpoint load, device allocation, bind, or network call merely by importing or constructing the app.
- GET /api/health returns a stable versioned readiness payload, and GET /api/config returns only sanitized public runtime/generation capabilities without filesystem secrets, environment values, raw conversation content, or live objects.

- Focused tests run without a real checkpoint, GPU, external network, or paid service.

title: Ship terminal chat modes, commands, and transcripts

Treat transcript export as a user-requested artifact separate from aggregate tracking: serialize the canonical versioned Conversation schema as strict UTF-8 JSONL, update atomically only after completed turns, and never place raw prompts or responses in metrics implicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts.chat accepts the checkpoint, device, one-shot -p/--prompt mode, and documented generation overrides; --help stays dependency-light and invalid combinations fail without a traceback.

title: Make ChatEngine termination and context bounds exact
description:
Harden the shared ChatEngine with exact chat-stage termination, deterministic context-window construction, and focused behavioral tests.

Plan ticket coverage: CLI-009 through CLI-011.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Derive assistant_end and BOS from the loaded tokenizer and pass both as an explicit stop-token set to the shared streaming generator. Treat sampled stops as control metadata, never visible assistant content. Build an observable context-window policy that retains the newest turns, drops oldest complete user/assistant turns first, and left-crops only the newest user's content tokens when the fixed chat controls plus that message cannot otherwise fit. Preserve the full uncropped transcript separately. Never split token IDs or synthesize a second chat template. Report dropped turns and truncated user tokens in ChatState so cropping is not silent.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every chat generation supplies exactly assistant_end plus BOS as its explicit stop-token set; the expected assistant_end and safety BOS IDs come from the loaded tokenizer.
- A sampled assistant_end or BOS ends generation immediately, is absent from visible token IDs, text deltas, assistant history, and transcript content, and remains observable through the terminal completion event's exact stop ID, reason, and sampled-token count.
- If neither stop appears, generation emits exactly max_new_tokens visible tokens and reports max_new_tokens completion with no stop ID.
- Deterministic ChatEngine tests cover an expected assistant_end, an unexpected BOS, and no stop before the configured limit, including immediate stops and the guarantee that no later model step is taken.
- Context construction drops oldest complete turns before truncating the newest user content, preserves required control tokens and the final assistant_start, leaves the full transcript unchanged, and reports all cropping in immutable state.
- Exact-fit, one-token-over, long-current-message, and multi-turn fixtures prove every model forward receives at most model.max_seq_len tokens and that an impossible fixed-control budget fails before model invocation.
- ChatEngine composes the shared generation API for all termination behavior; no CLI- or engine-specific duplicate sampling loop is introduced.
- Focused tests remain deterministic, network-free, GPU-independent, and cover state rollback after rendering, context, or generation failures.

title: Build the reusable ChatEngine and streaming contracts
description:
Turn the terminal-chat stub into a transport-agnostic inference boundary by integrating the existing SFT checkpoint loader, canonical chat renderer, GenerationConfig, and shared generator. Define immutable ChatState and TokenEvent contracts plus one ChatEngine lifecycle that terminal and web adapters can drive without owning token sampling.

Plan ticket coverage: CLI-001 through CLI-004.

Source of truth: plans/pre-training.md.
design: Reuse scratch_llm.config.GenerationConfig rather than adding a second generation-config type. Refactor or extend scratch_llm.generation only as needed to expose incremental single-sequence generation while preserving its existing batch APIs, explicit stop-token-set contract, stop-token omission, per-row determinism, and caller RNG/module-mode restoration. ChatEngine owns the loaded model/tokenizer, normalized full conversation history, renderer-derived completion prompts, UTF-8-safe incremental text assembly, immutable state snapshots, and one active generation transaction. Keep argparse and FastAPI imports outside the engine, and provide injected checkpoint/clock seams for deterministic CPU tests. A configured top_p must either be supported by the shared primitive or rejected before state mutation; it must never be silently ignored.

- scratch_llm.config.GenerationConfig remains the single canonical generation-settings contract; checkpoint defaults and explicit overrides validate temperature, top_k, max_new_tokens, seed, and any top_p behavior consistently.
- Frozen ChatState and TokenEvent values are transport-neutral and JSON-compatible, contain no live Torch objects, and expose enough checkpoint, renderer, token-count, text-delta, timing, and lifecycle metadata for both terminal and web consumers.
- ChatEngine loads and validates an SFT checkpoint through the existing model-only loader, infers the tokenizer from checkpoint metadata, places the model on the requested device in evaluation mode, and fails actionably on incompatible checkpoints.
